title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
prompt:
A playlist of read-aloud chapters is a singly linked list. Remove the n-th node from the end and return the head. Try to do it in one pass.

Write removeNthFromEnd(head, n). Helpers ListNode, fromArray, toArray are at the top; keep them.

  • toArray(removeNthFromEnd(fromArray([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]), 2)) gives [1, 2, 3, 5]
  • toArray(removeNthFromEnd(fromArray([1]), 1)) gives []
  • toArray(removeNthFromEnd(fromArray([1, 2]), 2)) gives [2] (removing the head)

Constraints: 1 to 30 nodes; 1 <= n <= length. Target: O(n) time, O(1) space.

tests.name: duplicate values: removes by position, not value

hints: Trigger: "n-th from the end" in a singly linked list (you can't walk backwards) = two pointers with a fixed gap. When the front one hits the end, the back one is n from the end.

To delete a node you need the node before it. Start both pointers at a dummy node in front of the head, move fast n + 1 steps ahead, then move both until fast is null. Now slow.next is the node to delete.

Shape:

const dummy = new ListNode(0, head);
let fast = dummy, slow = dummy;
for (let step = 0; step <= n; step++) fast = fast.next;
while (fast !== null) { fast = fast.next; slow = slow.next; }
slow.next = slow.next.next;
return dummy.next;
explain:
Time O(L) for a list of length L, one pass. Space O(1). The two-pass version (count the length, then walk to position L - n) is also O(L) and perfectly fine to say first; the gap trick just does it in one walk.

Say it: "I'll put a dummy before the head so removing the head isn't a special case, then use two pointers n + 1 apart. When the front pointer runs off the end, the back pointer sits right before the node to delete. One pass, O(1) space."
